settings.gate_rule_source: whip-lead, 2026-11-25 (after the gate-5 code review's MUST 1, reports/reviews/2026-11-25_review_e311-code.md): the planted pass that decides run 2 reads the floored exclusion; the literal App. E.2 reading is computed and reported beside it for every crosscoder. settings.floor_source: Floored exclusion (crosscoder.fold_floor, beta_floor): a scaled latent is dropped only when a base beta (eps_base or r_base, each on its own, both must clear) is below -m x sd_full. The 100k latent-scaling tokens are split into K = 10 folds of whole windows (each Pile row or task window wholly in one fold, windows assigned in a seeded random order; reviews/2026-11-25_review_e311-negbeta-floor.md MUST 3). Each fold gives the latent's base beta by the same closed form (beta_sums); the full-sample beta is about the mean of the K fold betas, so sd_full = sd(fold betas, unbiased) / sqrt(K), with K - 1 = 9 degrees of freedom. m = 3: for a latent whose true base beta is 0, P(beta < -3 sd_full) is the t(9) tail, 0.0075 per beta, at most 0.015 per latent for the two betas (against 0.10 for a two-half split's t(1), review MUST 2). Edge cases (tests/test_crosscoder_floor.py, all pass): sd 0 gives floor 0, the literal rule (beta >= 0); a latent with fewer than alive_min (10) firing tokens in any fold, or a non-finite fold beta, has an undefined sd and gets floor 0 (the literal rule; counted in beta_floor.undefined_*); a beta exactly at -floor is kept (as 0 is under the literal rule); a single latent needs no pooling. The approximation: fold betas are unweighted (each fold's denominator differs a little), so sd_full is approximate
